continuities.name: Kamen Rider: Showa continuity
continuities.description: The Showa-era series (1971–1989) share one continuity: recurring mentor and team-ups, the 1979 series declares all previous shows canonical, and Black RX brings back the ten previous Riders.
continuities.quote: The series from April 1971 to January 1976 (Kamen Rider, V3, X, Amazon, Stronger) included a recurring mentor, Tobei Tachibana, and also featured regular team-ups with each protagonist, with the exception of Amazon, with Hirayama stating "I was planning to save it until the next development, so I thought it was not necessary for a while, but the cancellation was decided." After a four-year hiatus following the finale of Kamen Rider Stronger, the series returned to broadcast television in October 1979 for two years with The New Kamen Rider (featuring Skyrider) and Kamen Rider Super-1. … The 1979 series was initially intended as a reboot of the original 1971 series of the same name, going back to the basic, essential themes established in that show, but eventually it was established that all the previous Kamen Rider shows were canonical to it, with previous Riders appearing. … Kamen Rider Black premiered in 1987, the first series since Amazon not hinting at a relationship to its predecessors. … In RX’s finale, the ten previous Riders returned to help Black RX defeat the Crisis Empire.

in_universe.label: Showa sequence
in_universe.quote: The series from April 1971 to January 1976 (Kamen Rider, V3, X, Amazon, Stronger) included a recurring mentor, Tobei Tachibana, and also featured regular team-ups with each protagonist, with the exception of Amazon, with Hirayama stating "I was planning to save it until the next development, so I thought it was not necessary for a while, but the cancellation was decided." After a four-year hiatus following the finale of Kamen Rider Stronger, the series returned to broadcast television in October 1979 for two years with The New Kamen Rider (featuring Skyrider) and Kamen Rider Super-1. … The 1979 series was initially intended as a reboot of the original 1971 series of the same name, going back to the basic, essential themes established in that show, but eventually it was established that all the previous Kamen Rider shows were canonical to it, with previous Riders appearing. … Kamen Rider Black premiered in 1987, the first series since Amazon not hinting at a relationship to its predecessors. … In RX’s finale, the ten previous Riders returned to help Black RX defeat the Crisis Empire.

continuities.name: Power Rangers (Mighty Morphin to Cosmic Fury)
continuities.description: One continuity from Mighty Morphin (1993) to Cosmic Fury (2023), including Alien Rangers, the Turbo movie and Once & Always.
continuities.quote: The first six seasons (beginning with Mighty Morphin Power Rangers and ending with In Space) followed an overarching, evolving storyline. … Although the seventh season, Lost Galaxy, had ties with the preceding season, it was otherwise the first season to follow a self-contained story, as would later seasons of the show up until the seventeenth, RPM. … The thirtieth season, Cosmic Fury, is a continuation of Dino Fury’s story. … According to executive producer Simon Bennett, Cosmic Fury was planned to be the final season set within the canon established since Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, with Hasbro instead opting for a franchise reboot; this reboot was originally set to be produced in partnership with Netflix; however, in 2024, Hasbro and Netflix ended their partnership, with the former opting to search for a new creative partner.
